desc_en: Data-driven global and regional weather forecasting, subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction, precipitation nowcasting and traffic spatiotemporal forecasting, plus a few LLM event-forecasting papers.
trend_en: Share up 29.8 → 42.3: AI weather models are moving to probabilistic forecasts and extreme-event evaluation (tropical cyclones, S2S), and a new branch trains LLM event-forecasting agents with RL.

desc_en: General-purpose non-LLM deep RL methods: representations and auxiliary tasks, plasticity loss, sample efficiency, offline-to-online, and large-scale parallel off-policy training.
trend_en: Share collapsed 65.1 → 17.7: RL attention has moved to RLVR and agentic RL for LLMs; the remaining work centres on replay-ratio scaling, plasticity and parallel training dynamics.

desc_en: Linear probes that read truth, beliefs, length planning and similar information from LLM hidden states, and tests of the probes' own reliability and confounders.
trend_en: Share up 16.2 → 26.0: probing has shifted from "what is in the representation" to safety uses: white-box activation monitoring, monitors that transfer across models, and detecting hidden bias and "knowing but not saying".

desc_en: Cross-domain papers grouped by the "we introduce a large-scale dataset/benchmark" phrasing (precipitation, cat vocalisations, counting, mass spectrometry); the topics do not cohere, so this is a wording cluster.
trend_en: Share fell sharply 58.5 → 14.9: dataset papers were absorbed by topic-specific clusters, diluting the generic-wording cluster; 2027 adds a meta-analysis of what makes a dataset paper valuable.

desc_en: Evaluation sets that test LLMs on one profession or skill: meteorology, law, materials, licensing exams, cultural norms, competitive programming.
trend_en: Share shrank 83.3 → 14.9: yet another domain-X QA benchmark adds little; evaluation is moving to LLM judges, agent benchmarks and evaluation platforms such as MathArena.

desc_en: Transformers with shared weights and looped layer blocks that use variable depth for latent reasoning and test-time compute scaling.
trend_en: Share up about 5× (7.1 → 34.9): after Huginn's recurrent depth and looped language models such as Ouro, this became a popular architecture; 2027 work tackles parallelism, memory, depth extrapolation and looped attention design.

desc_en: Improvements to PPO's clipped objective, trust regions, KL regularisation and policy-gradient variance, across continuous control, auction bidding and RLHF.
trend_en: Share up 31.3 → 40.9: instability in LLM RL has revived work on PPO clipping and trust-region surrogates, with variants such as power-law surrogates, α-divergences and directional clipping.

desc_en: Biases of LLMs acting as judges, their agreement with humans, rubric design and judge-panel selection.
trend_en: Share doubled 18.7 → 37.7: the focus moved from building better judges to psychometric-style audits (generalisability theory, rubric failure, tests without shared annotators) and rubric rewards for RL.

desc_en: World models built on video generators that accept camera or action control and generate explorable worlds in real time, along with their memory mechanisms.
trend_en: Share up more than 3× (15.6 → 52.8): driven by Genie 3-style playable world models; the 2027 focus is long-horizon spatial consistency through trajectory-indexed memory, persistent 3D Gaussian state and dedicated benchmarks.

desc_en: Graph representation learning, graph generation, link prediction, graph foundation models on text-attributed graphs, and LLMs reading graphs.
trend_en: Share down 59.1 → 43.9: classic GNN node classification is fading; growth is in foundation models for text-attributed graphs, graph vocabularies and graph tokens, and serialising neighbourhoods for LLMs.

desc_en: Evaluating and diagnosing perception and reasoning failures of vision-language models (counting, multi-image, long-tail, specialist imagery), with targeted fixes.
trend_en: Roughly stable, slightly down (52.5 → 45.3): fewer general VLM benchmarks and more diagnostic work on the gap between VLMs and specialist vision models, multi-image position bias and numerosity mechanisms.

desc_en: Removing specific knowledge, entities or hazardous capabilities from LLMs while preserving utility, and rigorous evaluation of whether unlearning worked.
trend_en: Share down 37.3 → 26.3: cooling after the 2026 peak; methods moved to layer- and subspace-localised unlearning and preventive capability locking, and evaluation now asks whether knowledge stays gone under relearning attacks.

desc_en: Low-bit quantization of LLM weights, activations and KV cache, quantization-aware training, vector quantization and low-precision (FP4) training.
trend_en: Share down 42.9 → 32.8: 4-bit PTQ is saturated; new work pushes 2-bit vector-quantization QAT, outlier analysis for NVFP4 pretraining and KV-quantization distillation for reasoning models.

desc_en: A mixed bag grouped by generic "neural network/architecture" wording: local and forward-only learning, width adaptation, optimizer reparameterisation and scattered applications.
trend_en: Share fell sharply 44.4 → 13.7: finer topic clusters split this generic-wording cluster in 2027; the most coherent remainder is local or forward learning as an alternative to backpropagation.

desc_en: Classical statistical learning theory: random matrices, ridge regression and sketching, covariance estimation, and asymptotics of heavy-tailed ERM.
trend_en: Share down 49.5 → 31.4: counts still grew but were diluted by the 2027 submission surge; new topics include explaining grokking through minimum-norm interpolation and theory for MAE.

desc_en: Scattered optimisation topics (multi-task gradient conflict, curvature proxies, loss normalisation) grouped by shared wording such as "exact/fixed/When does…"; a style cluster.
trend_en: Share jumped 20× (3.0 → 62.1): almost all are new 2027 papers with titles on the "When Does X Preserve Y?" template, likely homogenised writing from AI-assisted or automated research rather than a real new direction.

desc_en: Noise schedules, few-step samplers, score approximation and curse-of-dimensionality theory, and memorisation versus generalisation in diffusion models.
trend_en: Share down slightly 43.9 → 36.5: applied diffusion work moved to flow matching and application clusters, leaving few-step reverse-dynamics learning and statistical theory on low-dimensional structure.

desc_en: A loose group on AI's effects on labour, peer review, regulation and public perception, plus meta-research on AI scientists and AI reviewing.
trend_en: Share down 36.3 → 22.3: the 2026 interest in AI scientists and the social impact of agents was diluted; 2027 adds conference meta-research on the submission surge and AI reviewers replacing humans.

desc_en: Constructing jailbreak attacks on LLMs and VLMs, automated red-teaming and guardrail defences.
trend_en: Share halved 70.2 → 34.9: text-prompt jailbreak recipes are saturating; growth moved to decomposition attacks on agents, jailbreaks of embodied and full-duplex speech models, and the validity of red-teaming metrics.

desc_en: Multimodal fusion without large models: missing modalities, modality imbalance, sentiment analysis and multimodal medical diagnosis.
trend_en: Stable (49.5 → 46.7): still dominated by reliability-weighted modalities and imbalance correction, with applications spreading to brain-disease diagnosis and cancer survival prediction.

desc_en: Molecular representation learning, property prediction, force fields and quantum-chemistry functionals, and evaluation of molecular foundation models.
trend_en: Share down 38.4 → 29.5: pure graph representations are fading in favour of physics-informed representations such as electron density and molecular orbitals, and rigorous evaluation of molecular foundation models and LLM chemical reasoning.

desc_en: Linear attention, gated DeltaNet, associative memory, hybrid linear/softmax layers, and linearising pretrained LLMs.
trend_en: Share up 17.7 → 26.7: interest rose after Gated DeltaNet hybrids shipped in production models such as Qwen3-Next and Kimi Linear; 2027 work compensates for limited state memory and does on-policy linearisation.

desc_en: KV cache eviction, quantization, sparse reads and budget allocation for long-context inference.
trend_en: Share up 47.9 → 67.4: long chains of thought and agents made the KV cache the main bottleneck; 2027 turns to joint rate-distortion optimisation of eviction and quantization, decode-time budgets for reasoning models, and MLA/FP4 latent caches.

desc_en: Multivariate and long-horizon time series forecasting models, time series foundation models and evaluation protocols.
trend_en: Share down 99.9 → 77.9 but still the largest classic cluster in this packet: lightweight plug-in modules keep appearing, alongside rethinks of evaluation on irregular series and of whether foundation models are truly general.

desc_en: Client heterogeneity, personalisation, communication efficiency, asynchronous and split federated learning.
trend_en: Share keeps falling 93.9 → 61.4: classic heterogeneity-aware aggregation shows diminishing returns; remaining growth is in split FL, one-shot FL with pretrained models, and federated unlearning.

desc_en: Debate, collaboration topologies and communication protocols among LLM agents, including latent-space and KV-level communication.
trend_en: Share doubled 16.7 → 34.2: the focus moved from multi-agent debate to communication itself: latent communication, end-to-end learned communication, communication audits and collaboration on shared codebases.

desc_en: Self-supervised pretraining (MAE, JEPA, contrastive learning) and its transfer to ECG, wearables, 3D shapes and audio.
trend_en: Share recovered 30.3 → 43.5: LeJEPA and related work revived JEPA, and self-supervision is spreading into domain foundation models for wearable and medical signals and 3D shapes.

desc_en: RAG pipelines, graph RAG, multi-hop retrieval reasoning, and retrieval-poisoning attacks and defences.
trend_en: Share plunged 89.8 → 24.9: classic RAG-pipeline papers gave way to deep-research and search agents; what remains is graph-RAG poisoning, on-device RAG and speculative retrieval.

desc_en: Training tool-using and long-horizon LLM agents with multi-turn RL, including environment synthesis, credit assignment and training frameworks.
trend_en: Share up 20.2 → 36.3: the question moved from whether agents can be trained to scaling environments (synthesised executable environments, Claw-style general agents), asynchronous rollout frameworks and multi-turn critics.

desc_en: 3DGS-based novel view synthesis, feed-forward reconstruction, inverse rendering and dynamic or driving-scene reconstruction.
trend_en: Stable (31.8 → 29.8): the centre of gravity keeps moving from per-scene optimisation to pose-free feed-forward GS and surround-view 4D driving reconstruction; relighting and volumetric scattering are new niches.

desc_en: World Action Models (WAMs) that jointly predict future video or latent states and robot actions, using video-generation priors as policies.
trend_en: Share up 16× (4.5 → 73.7): "WAM" became the name of a new paradigm replacing VLM-backbone VLAs; 2027 work studies the action-world interface, latent futures and 3D-native WAMs.

desc_en: Distillation in which a student receives per-token teacher supervision on its own sampled trajectories (OPD), used for reasoning and agent post-training.
trend_en: Share 0.5 → 108.3, the largest increase in this packet: after Thinking Machines' 2025 OPD blog post it became standard in post-training; 2027 work calibrates teacher-student mismatch, unifies OPD with GRPO and studies black-box OPD.

desc_en: Text- and audio-driven human motion generation, human-object and human-human interaction, and motion editing and retargeting.
trend_en: Stable (44.4 → 45.1): methods are moving to flow matching and Riemannian-manifold representations, with new camera-aware and streaming spatial-audio generation and interaction policies for humanoid robots.

desc_en: Learning-theory results on PAC and query complexity, minimax rates, identifiability and lower bounds, written in highly formulaic language.
trend_en: Share up 10× (8.1 → 80.9): almost entirely new in 2027, with prominent "log/fixed/exact" wording; this may partly reflect AI-assisted proofs lowering the cost of theory papers, and partly style clustering.

desc_en: MoE routing and load balancing, expert pruning and skipping, expert offloading and expert-parallel inference.
trend_en: Share up 38.4 → 58.1: fine-grained MoE is now the default for open large models, and research moved from routing design to deployment: training-free reduction of active experts, expert prefetching and EP decoding.

desc_en: Invariant learning, generalisation under distribution shift, and predicting OOD performance without target data.
trend_en: Share more than halved 26.8 → 11.4: the classic invariant-risk-minimisation line is fading, with scattered moves to ARC-style rule induction and compositional generalisation in world models.

desc_en: Low-level restoration with diffusion priors: real-world image and video super-resolution, dehazing and low-light enhancement.
trend_en: Share down 30.3 → 19.8: one-step diffusion SR is mature and homogeneous; novelty lies in distribution-shift one-step SR and preserving key regions in video SR.

desc_en: Lp adversarial training, adversarial purification, certified robustness and analysis of adversarial-example features.
trend_en: Share fell sharply 52.0 → 22.1: adversarial training of image classifiers keeps fading, with a little movement to test-time defences for LVLMs and data-free adversarial training.

desc_en: Improvements to flow matching and rectified flow objectives, sampling step sizes and one-step generation, and variants on manifolds and scientific data.
trend_en: Share down slightly 36.3 → 29.1: now a standard tool spread across application clusters, this cluster keeps methodological refinements such as second-order flow matching, curvature-adaptive step sizes and one-step generation.

desc_en: Detecting and localising anomalies in multivariate time series by modelling normality through reconstruction, prediction or time-frequency features.
trend_en: Stable (17.7 → 14.2): still mostly reconstruction and time-frequency modelling, with new multi-agent LLM analysers and anomaly prediction rather than after-the-fact detection.

desc_en: Temporal grounding, dense captioning, spatiotemporal grounding and long-video reasoning in video MLLMs.
trend_en: Stable (33.8 → 36.3): RL fine-tuning is now standard for temporal grounding, with new frame-level time awareness, audio-visual omni-modal evidence grounding and forgetting prevention in long videos.

desc_en: Convergence rates of SGD, momentum and adaptive methods under heavy-tailed noise, generalised smoothness and nonconvex nonsmooth objectives.
trend_en: Share down 31.3 → 20.7: classic convergence analysis was diluted, with new convergence theory for matrix optimizers such as Muon (Schatten momentum).

desc_en: Human values in LLMs, pluralistic alignment, moral profiles and how post-training shapes value preferences.
trend_en: Share halved 23.2 → 10.9: fewer value benchmarks; remaining work formalises value theory, studies how post-training shapes value preferences, and examines anchors from narrow fine-tuning.

desc_en: Distribution-free conformal prediction sets: conditional and class-wise coverage, covariate and label shift, and online conformal.
trend_en: Share down slightly 39.9 → 30.5: methods are being refined (class-wise coverage, finite-sample geometry, in-context full conformal); LLM applications have not gone mainstream.

desc_en: Visual and video QA datasets and benchmarks for charts, documents, driving, science and emergency response.
trend_en: Share down slightly 52.0 → 43.2: fewer general VQA methods and more vertical diagnostic benchmarks (solar-panel inspection, long-tail driving, disaster-damage assessment).

desc_en: Referring expression comprehension, visual grounding in 3D scenes and fine-grained region alignment in VLMs.
trend_en: Share doubled 13.6 → 27.0: grounding is treated as the evidence step of VLM reasoning, with training-free 3D grounding agents, render-and-verify methods and polygon-level grounding benchmarks.

desc_en: A mixed cluster grouped by "generative modeling" wording: GANs, one-step generation via Wasserstein gradient flows, and crystal, CAD and dental-crown generation.
trend_en: Share down 43.4 → 28.4: finer topic clusters absorbed this generic-wording cluster; the recognisable new threads are one-step generation from Wasserstein gradient flows and reward alignment for few-step models.

desc_en: Training LLM reasoning with verifiable rewards (RLVR/GRPO): exploration, rollout diversity, advantage shaping and stability.
trend_en: Share up slightly 44.9 → 51.1, with growth slowing: after the wave of GRPO variants, work moved to exploration and prior lock-in and asynchronous off-policy training, and on-policy distillation drew away some attention.

desc_en: Direct training of SNNs, ANN-to-SNN conversion, spiking Transformers and energy-efficient neuromorphic inference.
trend_en: Share down 50.0 → 37.9: spiking Transformers and neuron-dynamics improvements remain common, but growth lags overall submissions.

desc_en: Zero-shot TTS, speech tokenizers and neural audio codecs, voice conversion and conversational speech generation.
trend_en: Share down 27.3 → 15.8: speech tokenizers are maturing; growth moved to multi-speaker dialogue generation and streaming causal-diffusion TTS, and speech is increasingly studied inside omni-modal models.

desc_en: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) that both understand and generate or edit images in a single model, studying visual tokenizers, architectures and synergy between the two abilities.
trend_en: Share down 39.4 → 23.0: after the 2026 burst of BAGEL/Janus/MetaQueries-style architectures, 2027 turns to analysing understanding-generation synergy, self-teaching and reflective correction, and closed-loop evaluation, with fewer new architectures.

desc_en: Protein sequence and structure design with diffusion, flow matching and protein language models, including inverse folding, antibody and peptide design, and generation of protein dynamics.
trend_en: Stable (34.8 → 36.3): the focus is moving from single-chain backbone generation to all-atom, multi-conformation and protein-complex design, cryo-EM-guided generation and test-time design.

desc_en: A mixed set grouped by abstract wording such as "feature/fusion/module": infrared-visible fusion, person re-identification, occupancy prediction, deraining and pathology; the topics are scattered, so this is a style cluster.
trend_en: Share diluted 47.9 → 35.8: module-stacking application papers lost share as total submissions surged, with no clear new paradigm in the content.

desc_en: Estimating average and heterogeneous treatment effects from observational data, with orthogonal and doubly robust meta-learners, unobserved confounding, partial identification and instrumental variables.
trend_en: Share down 36.8 → 27.4 though counts grew: the method line advances steadily to long-term effects, distributional outcomes, proximal causal inference and coupling with downstream decisions, untouched by the LLM wave.

desc_en: Multi-fingered dexterous grasping and manipulation, hand-object reconstruction and tactile sensing, with emphasis on turning human video and demonstrations into robot-usable data.
trend_en: Share up 16.7 → 27.4: the data bottleneck has produced many data engines that turn egocentric human video into dexterous-hand demonstrations, plus HOI generation for augmentation and tactile-field estimation.

desc_en: Computer-use and GUI agents that complete tasks on desktop, mobile and web interfaces, plus their training environments and benchmarks.
trend_en: Share down 21.7 → 13.0 though counts still grew: work moved from GUI grounding and general OS benchmarks to verifiable synthetic software environments and long-horizon tasks in professional software, and some moved to the memory and skills clusters.

desc_en: Long-term and external memory for LLM agents (writing, consolidation, retrieval, revision and conflict resolution) and security issues such as memory poisoning and provenance.
trend_en: Surged about 8× (7.6 → 64.2): memory went from a RAG add-on to the agent's core state, with many papers on memory governance, belief revision, experience reuse and diagnosing memory utility.

desc_en: Building, retrieving, composing and evolving reusable skills (skill files and procedural workflows) for LLM agents, plus security evaluations of skill overreach and malicious skills.
trend_en: A new cluster, from zero to 37.9: after Agent Skills became the standard interface of mainstream agent harnesses in late 2025, skill compilation, composition failures, skill staleness and skill supply-chain attacks quickly became their own direction.

desc_en: Training dynamics and generalisation of deep networks: loss-landscape geometry, sharpness-aware minimisation (SAM), grokking, mode connectivity and memorisation.
trend_en: Share down 30.8 → 21.2: classic small-model dynamics work was diluted; new papers give finer theoretical accounts such as Adam stability phase diagrams and curvature diagnostics.

desc_en: Classifier-free guidance and training-free guidance in diffusion and flow sampling: guidance-strength schedules, spatial adaptivity, theory and alternatives.
trend_en: Share down slightly 25.7 → 20.9: empirical CFG tweaks are saturated; 2027 work explains mode collapse and overshoot through optimal control, optimal transport and information theory.

desc_en: Game theory and multi-agent learning: equilibrium computation in zero-sum and Markov games, CFR, imperfect-information games, last-iterate convergence and contract design.
trend_en: Stable (40.9 → 41.4): the theory core is unchanged, with new work on symmetry reduction in Markov games, correlated equilibria and test-time RL for imperfect-information games.

desc_en: VLA policies that output robot actions from a VLM backbone, studying action chunking, flow-matching action heads, real-time inference and online RL fine-tuning.
trend_en: Share keeps rising 42.9 → 67.0: the question moved from how to build a VLA to deployment: real-time inference on consumer GPUs, action-chunk switching, robustness to camera viewpoint and real-world RL for streaming VLAs.

desc_en: Process reward models that score each step of a reasoning chain, and step-level verifiers, used for test-time search and RL training.
trend_en: Share halved 23.2 → 12.1: the post-o1 PRM wave gave way to outcome-based RLVR; remaining work covers unsupervised PRMs, deriving process supervision from outcome rewards and auditing PRM bias.

desc_en: Multi-view and deep clustering, focusing on missing and unaligned views and anchor graphs, with spectral clustering, contrastive learning and granular-ball representations.
trend_en: Stable, slightly up (31.8 → 37.7): a small traditional area that keeps publishing; novelty lies in fully unaligned views, budget-limited acquisition and federated multi-view clustering.

desc_en: Capability analysis, bias diagnosis, visual-encoder design and small benchmarks for general VLMs; the content is loose.
trend_en: Share fell sharply 54.5 → 19.5: general VLM research was split off into specialised clusters such as spatial reasoning, video and unified models, leaving native VLMs and visual-encoder training recipes.

desc_en: Differential privacy mechanism design, privacy accounting, DP-SGD, privacy auditing and DP synthetic data.
trend_en: Share down 52.0 → 36.7: this theory-heavy area did not grow with the submission surge; new work centres on one-run privacy auditing, end-to-end accounting for synthetic data and privacy amplification in LLM inference.

desc_en: LLM-based automated theorem proving in Lean 4 and similar systems, autoformalisation and formal-verification benchmarks.
trend_en: Stable, slightly up (32.3 → 35.1): moving from single-model provers to agentic proof development and revisable proof construction, plus checks on semantic fidelity of autoformalisation and frontier benchmarks.

desc_en: Architectural changes to ViTs: token allocation and merging, attention replacements, positional encoding, efficient inference and training recipes.
trend_en: Share halved 45.4 → 23.2: room for backbone innovation has narrowed; most remaining work is theoretical bounds for token merging, adaptive tokenisation and ViT-5-style modernised recipes.

desc_en: Catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity in continual and lifelong learning: replay, regularisation, modularity and continual learning for LLMs.
trend_en: Share down 69.7 → 50.4: classic class-incremental benchmark papers are fading; growth comes from continual learning for LLMs and mechanistic analysis of the stability-plasticity trade-off.

desc_en: Using LLMs for symbolic and numeric planning, robot task planning and long-horizon agent planning, often combined with classical search and behaviour trees.
trend_en: Share down 49.0 → 35.1: standalone planning work was drawn off by the agent memory and skills clusters; new questions are whether agents follow the plans they state and how to enforce safety constraints on planning.

desc_en: Methodology papers that audit evaluation itself: answer-extraction and scoring errors, benchmark leakage and shortcuts, measurement validity, preregistration and reproducibility; titles are highly similar in style.
trend_en: A large new cluster, from zero to 85.3: almost entirely from 2027, with concentrated keywords such as preregistration and measurement validity; it looks like a new evaluation-methodology submission category or batches of audit papers from automated research, and needs further checking.

desc_en: Methods and theory of teacher-student knowledge distillation, covering LLM reasoning distillation, multi-teacher distillation and compression of vision and medical models.
trend_en: Share down slightly 62.6 → 51.6: general KD was diluted; on the LLM side work moved to mid-training distillation, circuit-level distillation and analysis of how distillation works.

desc_en: Analysing LLM internal features and circuits with sparse autoencoders, activation patching and activation steering.
trend_en: Stable (18.7 → 17.9): the field moved from stacking SAE variants to methodological questions such as identifiability and whether steering reflects real mechanisms, and links to safety problems such as emergent misalignment.

desc_en: Learning robot manipulation policies: behaviour cloning, diffusion policies, action chunking, world-action models (WAMs) and policy reward evaluation.
trend_en: Share surged 15.1 → 53.9: world-action models and closed-loop policy improvement from deployment rollouts became hot topics, and humanoid whole-body control and offline RL methods such as Q-chunking joined the cluster.

desc_en: Evolutionary search with LLMs as mutation operators to design heuristics, solvers and programs automatically, for combinatorial optimisation, chip design and more.
trend_en: Share up 31.8 → 50.2: the AlphaEvolve/FunSearch paradigm has been widely reproduced; attention moved to using failure feedback, when to reflect, uncertainty calibration and runtime-aware solver design.

desc_en: Concept-based interpretable models (CBMs): concept discovery, interventions, information leakage, and concepts generated by CLIP or LLMs.
trend_en: Stable (24.2 → 23.2): continued work on unsupervised concept sparsity, spatially grounded concepts and the harms of partial interventions, extending to pathology and robotics.

desc_en: Planning, perception and simulation for end-to-end autonomous driving, including driving VLAs, world models, closed-loop benchmarks and traffic simulation.
trend_en: Share up 62.1 → 75.6: driving VLAs merging with world-action models became mainstream, with more closed-loop evaluation (the Bench2Drive family) and self-play policies trained without expert demonstrations.

desc_en: Training, parallel decoding, remasking strategies and reasoning ability of masked and discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs).
trend_en: Share keeps growing 59.1 → 76.5: after LLaDA, Mercury and Gemini Diffusion the area entered an engineering phase, focused on block diffusion, dependency-aware parallel decoding and inference-time search and repair.

desc_en: MCTS planning and sequential Monte Carlo methods for RL, LLM reasoning search, combinatorial optimisation and diffusion sampling, with some sampling theory mixed in.
trend_en: Share halved 36.8 → 17.9: the 2024–25 wave of tree search for LLM reasoning has receded as RL post-training replaced explicit search; what remains improves MCTS algorithms themselves.

desc_en: Representation learning and foundation models for single-cell transcriptomics and gene expression, including multi-omics, perturbation prediction and cell annotation.
trend_en: Stable (24.7 → 21.9): the focus moved from training larger scFMs to questioning their value through in-vivo evaluation, a modality-translation view and combination with LLM-retrieved evidence.

desc_en: Structured and layer pruning of neural networks and LLMs, sparsity allocation and retraining-free compression.
trend_en: Share more than halved 63.6 → 28.1: pruning gains lose out to quantization and small-model distillation; 2027 work is mostly incremental, on cross-layer sparsity allocation and on-device dynamic pruning.

desc_en: Variational quantum circuits, quantum neural networks, barren plateaus, quantum error-correction decoding and hybrid quantum-classical models.
trend_en: Stable (35.3 → 36.5): the main line is still mitigating barren plateaus and improving trainability, with new hybrid applications such as quantum adapters for LLMs and quantum RAG.

desc_en: Evaluating and improving 3D spatial reasoning and spatial intelligence in VLMs and MLLMs: multi-view, reference frames, mental rotation and egocentric reasoning.
trend_en: Share up 31.8 → 47.4: spatial intelligence became the biggest weakness of MLLMs, with a flood of benchmarks (multi-view, panoramic, predictive spatial reasoning) and the start of training with RL and auxiliary-view distillation.

desc_en: Analysis papers grouped by wording such as "representation geometry/local structure/diagnostic", ranging from LoRA geometry to Fisher information to typographic art; a style cluster.
trend_en: Jumped from 3.5 to 57.7: almost all from 2027 with highly uniform title style, likely batch-produced analysis papers similar to the evaluation-audit cluster rather than one new research direction.

desc_en: Neural operators such as FNO that learn PDE solution operators, as surrogates for fluid dynamics, finite elements and other scientific computing.
trend_en: Share up sharply 33.8 → 57.9: scientific ML submissions expanded, with new operator architectures (Radon, Green's-function and latent-space operators), moving interfaces and stable long rollouts as selling points.

desc_en: Mechanisms, compression and efficiency of chain-of-thought reasoning, implicit and latent-space reasoning, and CoT faithfulness and monitorability.
trend_en: Share halved 87.3 → 40.5: after the 2026 wave of efficient reasoning and CoT compression, 2027 turns to CoT monitorability and faithfulness and to non-autoregressive latent reasoning with looped Transformers.

desc_en: Mostly instruction-based image, video and 3D editing with diffusion and flow models, with some LLM knowledge-editing (model editing) papers mixed in.
trend_en: Stable (80.3 → 72.1): image editing has moved to multi-turn long-horizon editing, canvas interaction and MLLM planning with DiT execution, while the share of LLM knowledge editing shrinks.

desc_en: Memory inside the model: associative memory, recurrent memory, test-time-trained memory layers and pluggable parametric memory modules.
trend_en: Share up 17.2 → 30.9: driven by Titans-style test-time learning and memory decoders, research moved from external retrieval to writable parametric and associative memory and its forgetting.

desc_en: Segmentation, change detection, change captioning and multispectral foundation models for remote-sensing imagery.
trend_en: Share up 21.2 → 32.3: remote-sensing tasks are being recast for MLLMs, with instruction-driven segmentation, reasoning-based change detection and any-band foundation models as the new main line.

desc_en: Safe RL under constrained MDPs: Lagrangian methods, hard constraints, chance constraints, control barrier functions and offline safe RL.
trend_en: Share down slightly 21.2 → 18.6: methods are stable; novelty lies in tail-risk controllability, variance-optimal replay and LLM-assisted synthesis of barrier functions.

desc_en: LLM safety alignment: over-refusal, alignment degradation from harmful fine-tuning, safety patches, steering and safety of reasoning models.
trend_en: Share down 63.6 → 50.9: interest in jailbreak defences fell; the focus moved to benign fine-tuning that breaks alignment, transferable safety patches and self-recovery within reasoning traces.

desc_en: Reward design for RL post-training: rubric rewards, reward shaping and reward models, and detecting and mitigating reward hacking.
trend_en: Share up 42.9 → 49.5: once RLVR extended to non-verifiable tasks, rubric-based RL became mainstream, followed by many studies of its reward hacking and over-optimisation.

desc_en: Systems, environments and benchmarks for recursive self-improvement (RSI), in which LLM agents improve by rewriting their own harness, data or workflows.
trend_en: A new cluster, from 1.0 to 37.4: RSI moved from thought experiment to an experimental topic, with dedicated environments (RSI-Env), code-level benchmarks and attribution-guided self-improvement of multi-agent workflows.

desc_en: Learning to solve TSP, VRP, MILP and other combinatorial optimisation problems with GNNs, RL and diffusion, and generalising across problem scales.
trend_en: Share down 52.5 → 39.8: pure neural solvers lost ground to LLM-generated heuristics (see the evolutionary algorithm-design cluster); remaining work targets scale generalisation and problem-duality augmentation.

desc_en: Modelling working memory, neural dynamics and cognitive mechanisms with recurrent networks, including reservoir computing and identifiability analysis.
trend_en: Share down slightly 24.7 → 20.5: a stable small community focused on aligning small RNNs with cognitive mechanisms and on phase transitions in learning dynamics.

desc_en: Regret bounds and algorithms for multi-armed, linear and generalised linear, and contextual bandits, including Thompson sampling and best-arm identification.
trend_en: Stable (36.8 → 37.4): this classic theory area holds its share, with new variants such as single-index models, semiparametric model selection and strategic agents.

desc_en: Zero-shot and trained detection of machine-generated text, attribution to source models, and paraphrase attacks that evade detection.
trend_en: Share down 26.2 → 17.9: detection performance is hitting a ceiling; research moved to length obfuscation, text from mixed models, Chinese detection benchmarks and theory of detector reliability.

desc_en: Reworking LLM supervised fine-tuning objectives, data selection, and post-training pipelines that unify or connect SFT and RL.
trend_en: Share down 48.5 → 34.4: after a burst of SFT-RL unification methods in 2026, 2027 focuses on RL-ready initialisation problems such as SFT-induced diversity collapse and preserving plasticity.

desc_en: Merging several fine-tuned models with no or light training: task vectors, interference removal, subspace alignment and continual merging.
trend_en: Share down slightly 30.3 → 23.0: task-interference models are converging; new directions are continual merging, on-device LoRA merging and preventing unauthorised merging.

desc_en: Discovering symbolic expressions and governing equations (ODEs/PDEs) from data, combining genetic programming with LLM-guided search.
trend_en: Stable (16.7 → 18.4): LLM-guided symbolic regression is now the default setup, and new work centres on search control, residual guidance and multi-objective evolution.

desc_en: A miscellany grouped by "LLM/large language model" wording: fingerprinting and provenance, knowledge gaps, code generation, routing and synthetic data; the topics do not cohere, so this is a wording cluster.
trend_en: Share plunged 98 → 25: generic "use an LLM for X" papers were drawn into new 2027 clusters (coding agents, OPSD, steering and others), leaving scattered topics such as model fingerprints and lineage.

desc_en: Architecture papers that modify softmax, linear or higher-order attention, multi-head structure and attention sinks, including complexity and expressivity analysis.
trend_en: Share down 42 → 28: counts still grow, but novelty is in details such as higher-order attention, sink removal and FP8 or quantized softmax, while generic new-attention proposals are diluted.

desc_en: Deep-network models of fMRI responses in visual cortex: brain-model representational alignment, visual reconstruction decoding, cross-subject alignment and connectome foundation models.
trend_en: Share down slightly 50 → 41: moving from image reconstruction to cross-subject alignable representations, in-silico interventions and questioning the reliability of encoding models (low-rank brains).

desc_en: In-context learning in LLMs: demonstration selection and ordering, task vectors, hypothesis selection in ICL and attention-based explanations, with a few extensions to VLAs and medical vision.
trend_en: Share fell sharply 42 → 17: prompt engineering such as demonstration retrieval and ordering is fading; remaining work turns to task vectors and mechanistic explanation as the reasoning and RL paradigm sidelines the topic.

desc_en: TabPFN-style prior-fitted networks and tabular foundation models: in-context prediction, scaling to large tables, tabular data generation and adapting to distribution shift.
trend_en: Share recovered 28 → 43: TabPFN v2 and later open models became the new base; papers moved from asking whether fine-tuning helps to extending context (Mixture-of-Contexts), mechanisms and relational data.

desc_en: De novo 2D and 3D molecule generation, fragment-based generation and structure-based drug design with diffusion, flow matching, BFNs and chemical language models.
trend_en: Share roughly stable (23 → 22): new trends are reward design and post-training for molecular generators, and fragment-level, multiscale 3D generation.

desc_en: New parameter-efficient fine-tuning structures and initialisations: LoRA variants, spectral and directional decompositions, block composition and rank adaptation, for LLMs and vision models.
trend_en: Share down 26 → 21: LoRA variants are saturating, prompting "are PEFT methods really different?" critiques and theoretical attempts such as function-space and curvature-based initialisation.

desc_en: Learning causal graphs and DAGs from observational data: constraint- and score-based methods, latent confounding, identifiability, and Bayesian and differentiable causal discovery.
trend_en: Share slowly down 33 → 26: the main line is stable, with new work on LLMs as priors or experts guiding causal discovery, target-centred subgraphs and high-dimensional Bayesian extensions.

desc_en: Design and convergence analysis of deep-learning optimizers: Adam variants, momentum, parameter-free adaptive methods and the orthogonalising Muon optimizer.
trend_en: Share halved 34 → 15: after the 2026 Muon wave the area is digesting, with papers filling in theory such as Muon generalisation analysis and Adam regret bounds, and new-optimizer proposals diluted.

desc_en: Mostly multimodal emotion recognition, mixed with action recognition, face recognition, wearable activity recognition and fine-grained recognition.
trend_en: Share down slightly 33 → 29: emotion recognition is now done with MLLMs plus cross-modal chain of thought or reward injection, with emphasis on interpretability and open vocabularies.

desc_en: Detecting and mitigating LLM hallucination: detectors based on internal representations, uncertainty, attention-head interventions and SAE features, plus hallucination benchmarks.
trend_en: Share down 39 → 25: methods have become homogeneous; 2027 brings meta-analyses of what hallucination benchmarks actually measure and debunking of topological detectors.

desc_en: Credit assignment in RL for long-horizon multi-turn LLM agents: step- and action-level advantage estimation, hindsight credit and dependency-aware policy optimisation.
trend_en: Share up sevenfold (12 → 87): RL training moved from single-turn maths reasoning to long-horizon agents in terminals and search, making step-wise credit assignment under sparse outcome rewards the core problem.

desc_en: Autoregressive and streaming long-video diffusion: Self Forcing-style training, KV cache management, real-time interactive generation and long-horizon consistency.
trend_en: Share tripled 13 → 38: Self Forcing, Rolling Forcing and LongLive opened the real-time long-video paradigm, followed in 2027 by many "X Forcing" variants and KV-cache and memory-compression work.

desc_en: Sample selection under labelling budgets: batch active learning, active feature acquisition, Bayesian experimental design and cost-aware annotation.
trend_en: Stable (18 → 20): new details include combining with prediction-powered inference (PPI) and zero-pool or metadata-only selection, settings closer to real budget constraints.

desc_en: GNN architectures and theory: message passing, directed graphs, memorisation and expressivity analysis, mixed with molecular and spatial-network applications.
trend_en: Share halved 49 → 18: general GNN architecture innovation is fading as graph learning is drawn off by graph foundation models, LLMs and specific scientific applications.

desc_en: ASR, speech-LLM bridging, full-duplex spoken dialogue models, TTS evaluation and paralinguistic understanding.
trend_en: Stable (32 → 32): the focus moved from ASR datasets to real-time full-duplex speech models and interaction problems such as routing and self-listening.

desc_en: Mutual information estimation, the information bottleneck and information-theoretic generalisation bounds, with applications to representation learning and privacy.
trend_en: Share down 20 → 13: this established theoretical tool keeps drifting to the margins; remaining work centres on discrete-bridge and diffusion-based MI estimation and change-of-measure inequalities.

desc_en: Time series forecasting: zero-shot prediction and ensembling with time series foundation models, retrieval-augmented forecasting, online correction under delayed feedback and forecasting agents.
trend_en: Share jumped 19 → 53: partly because forecasting split off from the general time-series cluster (144), and partly because ensembling and correcting frozen TSFMs and LLM-agent forecasting became new hot spots.

desc_en: Grouped by the word "event": temporal point processes and Hawkes modelling, neuromorphic event-camera vision and document event extraction; the topics are disjoint.
trend_en: Share roughly stable (14 → 17): on the point-process side, foundation models across event logs appeared; on the event-camera side, work moved to distilling encoders from RGB foundation models.

desc_en: Loss design, negative sampling, geometric properties and theory of InfoNCE/CLIP-style contrastive learning, including graph and multimodal contrastive learning.
trend_en: Share halved 41 → 21: fewer new contrastive methods, with a shift to explanatory work on CLIP geometry, hard-negative theory and limits of identifiability.

desc_en: Grouped by "neural network" wording: network verification, Lipschitz estimation, initialisation and wide-network theory, Hamiltonian networks and more; the topics are scattered.
trend_en: Share down 41 → 24: general network theory and verification work was diluted by large-model topics; verification moved to tighter bounds such as scalable Lipschitz estimation.

desc_en: RLHF from human preferences: reward-model training, reward over-optimisation and reward hacking, noisy feedback and interpretable rewards.
trend_en: Share collapsed 44 → 13: classic preference RLHF was replaced by verifiable rewards (RLVR), rubric rewards and on-policy self-distillation; remaining work centres on mitigating reward hacking.

desc_en: Repository-level software-engineering agents: SWE-bench-style long-horizon benchmarks, build-from-scratch and migration tasks, context compression and failure prediction.
trend_en: Share up ninefold (7 → 66): with Claude Code and Codex-style products in wide use, SWE-bench is saturated and many new "SWE-X" benchmarks move to million-line legacy codebases, long multi-turn work and building repositories from scratch.

desc_en: Group-equivariant networks, symmetry breaking and discovery, geometric-algebra networks, and scientific applications such as interatomic potentials and crystal generation.
trend_en: Share down 29 → 22: equivariant architectures keep being refined (geometric algebra, Weyl algebra), but critical benchmarks on "symmetry slippage" and calibrated equivariance have started to appear.

desc_en: Per-token distillation in which a model, on its own rollouts, uses itself with privileged information (reference answers or reflections) as teacher, replacing or supplementing RLVR.
trend_en: A new cluster, from 0 to 52: after on-policy distillation and OPSD were proposed in late 2025, many 2027 papers study selective distillation, entropy overshoot and privileged-information interventions, and extend the method to VLMs and cross-lingual settings.

desc_en: Continual learning with low-rank adapters: subspace protection, adapter routing and merging, to reduce catastrophic forgetting in LLMs and VLMs.
trend_en: Share up 12 → 18: the main arena of continual learning moved from rehearsal to LoRA libraries and subspace geometry, with new settings such as adapter routing and arbitration.

desc_en: Medical vision-language models: radiology report generation, CT and X-ray understanding, medical VQA benchmarks and clinical diagnostic reasoning.
trend_en: Share down 59 → 43: counts still grow, but the focus moved from 2D chest X-ray reports to 3D CT, multi-tool medical agents and evidence-aligned diagnosis.

desc_en: Selecting instruction-tuning data (coresets, gradient and information-gain selection) and evaluating instruction following, including visual instruction tuning.
trend_en: Share down 24 from 33: SFT data selection still produces papers but is squeezed by RL and distillation post-training; instruction-following evaluation moved to multi-turn constraints and omni-modal settings.

desc_en: Web and deep-search agents trained with RL: evidence filtering and verification, process rewards, synthesis of shortcut-resistant training tasks and multimodal search.
trend_en: Share up 18 → 26: the Search-R1/DeepResearch line has matured, and the focus moved from whether agents can search to admitting evidence, resolving conflicts and rubric-based process rewards.

desc_en: Non-LLM deep RL: actor-critic, distributional RL, model-based control such as TD-MPC, and analysis of Q-learning bias.
trend_en: Share up slightly (23 → 27): classic control RL holds its ground, with action chunking and TD-MPC improvements as new hot spots.

desc_en: General multimodal LLMs: visual encoders and projectors, information flow between modalities, text dominance and a range of understanding benchmarks.
trend_en: Share plunged 70 → 29: generic MLLM architecture and perception papers were drawn off by finer clusters such as video understanding, multimodal reasoning and OPSD.

desc_en: Self-supervised foundation models for EEG, cross-subject transfer and BCI decoding such as motor imagery, including EEG-fNIRS fusion and benchmarks.
trend_en: Share up 44 → 56: EEG foundation models (after LaBraM and CBraMod) are now standard; 2027 focuses on tokenizer design, layer-wise interpretability and EEG benchmarks for LLMs.

desc_en: Retrieval-augmented generation and multi-hop QA: evidence-chain retrieval, GraphRAG, parametric RAG and domain QA.
trend_en: Stable (23 → 21): the focus moved from passage relevance to evidence sufficiency and budgeted retrieval, and the boundary with the search-agent cluster is blurring.

desc_en: Discovering circuits and algorithmic mechanisms inside Transformers (arithmetic, toy tasks), including transcoders and training dynamics.
trend_en: Share up slightly (29 → 33): the field moved from finding single circuits to testing the consistency and faithfulness metrics themselves, with critiques of circuit benchmarks.

desc_en: Evaluating multi-turn LLM interaction: user simulators, multi-turn sycophancy and intent drift, role-play and benchmarks of conversational naturalness.
trend_en: Share up slightly (30 → 34): "LLMs get lost in multi-turn conversation" prompted follow-ups, and the realism and validity of user simulators became a research topic in their own right.

desc_en: ANN search for vector databases: graph indexes, IVF partition routing, hashing, filtered search and MIPS.
trend_en: Share halved 10 → 5: a small stable community whose counts are flat and diluted by the total; new topics are stability of filtered and multi-vector search and hubness analysis.

desc_en: Filtering, rewriting and synthesising LLM pretraining data, curriculum ordering, repetition and continued pretraining, and low-cost pretraining of small models.
trend_en: Share down slightly 31 → 25: the main line became generative curation that rewrites and recycles low-quality web text, replacing classifier-based quality filtering.

desc_en: A wording cluster: many abstracts use the same stock phrases ("evidence/audit/held fixed/paired/matched") across selective prediction, model selection and medical case studies; not a single research direction.
trend_en: 561 papers (130 per 10k) appeared from nothing in 2027: the highly formulaic "audit/evidence" writing likely comes from a wave of AI-assisted or automatically generated submissions and deserves a separate quality check.

desc_en: Mitigating shortcut learning and spurious correlations: worst-group robustness, debiasing without group labels, feature geometry and masking SAE concepts.
trend_en: Share down 12 → 7: classic Waterbirds-style debiasing is fading; new work uses SAEs and weight editing to handle spurious features in LLM reasoning.

desc_en: Speculative decoding for faster LLM inference: draft-model training, parallel drafting, relaxed acceptance rules, batching and edge-cloud collaboration.
trend_en: Share up 36 → 53: inference cost became the deployment bottleneck, and parallel drafting, lenient verification and self-speculation in diffusion language models became new directions.

desc_en: Wasserstein and group DRO and their applications to regression, survival analysis and decision learning, with a few miscellaneous robustness papers.
trend_en: Stable (12 → 11): new details combine DRO with decision-focused learning and with missing-data mask spaces.

desc_en: Personalising LLMs and agents to user preferences: user-profile modelling, personalised rewards and evaluation, and long-term interaction memory.
trend_en: Stable (27 → 28): moving from single-turn preference adaptation to evolving long-term user state and memory benchmarks for personal assistants.

desc_en: TCS-style papers on learning-augmented algorithms with predictions, approximation and online algorithms, submodular maximisation and fair clustering.
trend_en: Share down 34 → 19: pure algorithms papers are flat in number and diluted; learning-augmented settings extend to new problems such as facility location and dense subgraphs.

desc_en: Controlling LLM behaviour at inference by adding direction vectors to the residual stream: multi-attribute steering, prefix steering, safety and sycophancy control, and representation engineering.
trend_en: Share doubled 27 → 59: steering became a lightweight tool for alignment and control; 2027 work looks at a data perspective, minimum-KL steering and learning steering vectors from scalar rewards alone.

desc_en: General time series analysis: classification, irregular multivariate series, generation and imputation, time-series-language alignment and pretraining time series foundation models.
trend_en: Share down 71 → 42: forecasting split off into cluster 117, and new directions in the remainder include time-series-language alignment and caption generation.

desc_en: DUSt3R/VGGT-style feed-forward multi-view and monocular 3D/4D reconstruction, including long sequences, metric scale, articulated objects and human-scene reconstruction.
trend_en: Share nearly doubled 27 → 50: feed-forward geometric foundation models such as VGGT replaced per-scene optimisation, and 2027 builds on them with long sequences, view graphs and post-optimisation.

desc_en: Identity-preserving human video generation: audio-driven talking heads, portrait and dance animation, multi-person references and virtual try-on.
trend_en: Share lost two-thirds 31 → 11: once open video base models (Wan and others) shipped with reference conditioning, dedicated digital-human pipelines were absorbed by general video generation and autoregressive streaming generation.

desc_en: Generative flow-matching and diffusion policies for online and offline RL: Q-guidance, critic gradients, one-step and MeanFlow policies, and fine-tuning.
trend_en: Share up 13 → 20: flow policies became the new default policy class in RL and robot control, with focus on test-time Q-guidance and training under multi-step budgets.

desc_en: General RL post-training for LLM reasoning: GRPO variants, off-policy RL, the exploration-stability trade-off, reward saturation and training efficiency.
trend_en: Share down 80 → 25: the 2026 GRPO wave has split into finer clusters such as credit assignment and OPSD; remaining work argues RL is mere "sparse policy selection" and turns to off-policy training and numerical stability.

desc_en: Generalising to unseen target domains: domain-invariant representations, style augmentation, MoE subset invariance and domain-generalisation theory.
trend_en: Share down 20 → 12: classic DG benchmark work is fading; remaining papers lean theoretical (Rademacher bounds, identifiability) or federated.

desc_en: Object and relation hallucination in LVLMs and MLLMs, mostly addressed by training-free contrastive decoding, attention reallocation and representation editing to strengthen visual evidence.
trend_en: Stable (31 → 29); training-free decoding interventions still dominate, but 2027 brings placebo-controlled re-checks and "hallucination routing" diagnostic benchmarks that question the real gains of existing methods.

desc_en: Variational inference, Bayesian neural networks, Gaussian processes and simulation-based inference, centred on neural posterior estimation and amortised inference.
trend_en: Share keeps falling (36 → 24); classic VI and BNNs are fading, and remaining growth comes from amortised inference and in-context, prior-fitted Bayesian inference.

desc_en: Shortening the chains of thought of large reasoning models: length rewards, early stopping, reflection control, reasoning compression and latent reasoning.
trend_en: Down after the 2026 o1/R1 surge (58 → 34); coarse length penalties are saturated, and 2027 turns to early stopping by convergence detection, entropy-aware reflection rewards and metacognitive controllers.

desc_en: Unsupervised skill discovery and hierarchical RL based on mutual information and empowerment, learning reusable, composable behaviour primitives.
trend_en: Stable (9.6 → 10.0); methods are converging on trajectory-level objectives and capacity scaling, with new LLM-guided hierarchical skills and parameterised motor skills discovered for VLAs.

desc_en: Merging, selecting or resampling visual tokens in video and multimodal LLMs to cut long-video inference cost, mostly training-free.
trend_en: Share nearly doubled (15 → 27); driven by inference cost of long-video and omni-modal LLMs, with global codebooks, joint frame-budget allocation and audio-visual token compression, and one paper pointing to selection bias in evaluation.

desc_en: Low-level restoration such as denoising, deblurring, deraining and low-light enhancement, centred on all-in-one models that handle many degradations.
trend_en: Stable (30 → 32); all-in-one remains the main axis, with new one-step flow restorers, MoE routing and agentic RL restoration, extending to infrared, polarisation and surgical images.

desc_en: Evaluation of multilingual LLMs, cross-lingual transfer, low-resource language benchmarks and cultural bias.
trend_en: Share halved (52 → 23); general multilingual benchmarks saturated after the 2026 boom, and 2027 turns to benchmarks for minority languages (Yi), flaws in translation evaluation and cross-lingual RL and self-distillation.

desc_en: Collaboration topologies, role assignment, orchestration and training of LLM multi-agent systems, plus MAS benchmarks and fault tolerance.
trend_en: Stable at a high level (56 → 58); moving from hand-designed collaboration structures to self-evolving MAS, capability-aware orchestration and joint post-training of heterogeneous agents.

desc_en: LLM agents for research ideation, paper reproduction, algorithm discovery and research evaluation, including studies of peer review.
trend_en: Nearly doubled (36 → 65); amid the AI Scientist/AlphaEvolve wave, evaluation expanded from single-point reproduction to full research trajectories as evidence evolves, open problems and paper reconstruction.

desc_en: Scaling laws for pretraining and fine-tuning: compute-optimal allocation, batch size and step count, hyperparameter transfer and theoretical explanations of scaling laws.
trend_en: Share down (43 → 34); moving from parameter-data laws to new scaling axes such as training steps and batch size, fitting performance from configuration, and "data-task alignment".

desc_en: Camera and motion control, video editing, and temporal and geometric consistency in video diffusion models.
trend_en: Share halved (66 → 33); video generation was drawn off by world models, 4D and embodied work, leaving unified camera and motion control and consistency via geometry distillation.

desc_en: Model-based RL and latent world models (including JEPA-style ones) for imagined rollouts, MPC and long-horizon planning.
trend_en: Up 3.4× (21 → 72); world models became a mainstream topic, and 2027 work studies audits of action identifiability, variable-length latent prediction, language world models and decision certification.

desc_en: Theory of implicit bias in GD and SGD, the edge of stability, saddle-to-saddle dynamics, large step sizes and feature learning.
trend_en: Share down (35 → 27); the problem set is stable (EoS, flat minima, diagonal linear networks), with new analyses of in-context learning dynamics in softmax attention.

desc_en: Architecture and training of image diffusion models: DiT, representation alignment (REPA-style), pixel-space diffusion and faster sampling.
trend_en: Keeps falling (45 → 31); general diffusion methods are drawn off by flow matching, and the hot spots inside the cluster are VAE-free pixel-space DiTs and representation guidance.

desc_en: Monocular, video and stereo depth estimation and depth completion, with emphasis on metric scale and depth foundation models.
trend_en: Down slightly (21 → 17); fewer new foundation models after Depth Anything 3, with work moving to calibration from sparse measurements, temporal consistency in long videos and heterogeneous cameras.

desc_en: Safety and failures of LLM multi-agent systems: denial of service, defection, privacy leakage, spread of adversarial influence, role integrity and failure attribution.
trend_en: An emerging direction (5 → 44, about 9×); as MAS are deployed, research moved from whether agents can collaborate to how system-level risks grow with scale and how to calibrate shared memory.

desc_en: Group and counterfactual fairness, debiasing sensitive attributes, fairness audits and measuring social bias.
trend_en: Share halved (40 → 18); traditional debiasing methods are fading, and remaining work turns to impossibility theory, methodology for bias evaluation and instruction-style bias in LLM agents.

desc_en: Inference-time compute scaling with parallel sampling, self-consistency voting, verifiers and sequential revision.
trend_en: Down slightly from a high level (59 → 52); moving from best-of-N and voting to coordinated sequential and parallel planning, modelling verifier flaws and attributing gains to coverage versus selection.

desc_en: Using LLM agents to simulate human and social behaviour, user simulators, and evaluating theory of mind and social reasoning.
trend_en: Share down (44 → 31); moving from "can LLMs simulate humans" benchmarks to audits of simulation validity (identifiability, testing behavioural hypotheses, persona grounding).

desc_en: Conditional, discrete and geometric flow matching and applications to deblurring, single-cell trajectories, RNA and physical fields.
trend_en: Nearly doubled (28 → 55); flow matching replaced diffusion as the default generative framework, with many extensions to Lie groups, geometric manifolds and scientific data.

desc_en: Posterior sampling with diffusion and flow models as priors for computational imaging and scientific inverse problems.
trend_en: Roughly stable (37 → 34); extending DPS-style guidance to PnP-ADMM with flow priors, few-step MCMC, nonlinear blind inverse problems and evaluation protocols.

desc_en: Classic XAI: Shapley/SHAP feature attribution, interaction attribution and evaluation of attribution methods.
trend_en: Keeps receding (16 → 11); classic XAI is squeezed by mechanistic interpretability, and remaining work centres on Shapley interaction structure, amortised estimation and the methodological point that attribution evaluation needs ablations.

desc_en: VLA policies for robot manipulation: execution correction, failure recovery, RL fine-tuning, inference speed-up and robustness diagnosis.
trend_en: Exploded (6 → 55, about 10×); after π0 and OpenVLA spread, VLAs became the main line in robotics, and 2027 focuses on inference-time correction and backtracking for frozen VLAs and flaws in benchmarks.

desc_en: Environments, benchmarks, reliability and safety guardrails for LLM agents, including deception, asynchronous execution and robustness on long-horizon tasks.
trend_en: More than doubled (32 → 71); evaluation moved from task success rates to behavioural properties such as certifying evaluability under nondeterminism, deception under pressure and interference from user revisions.

desc_en: Improvements to training, representations and spectral structure of PINNs and neural PDE solvers.
trend_en: Share down (53 → 30); PINN training tricks are saturating, with new PDE-solving agents and benchmarks for solver generation.

desc_en: Behaviour cloning, adversarial imitation, inverse RL and learning rewards and policies from (suboptimal) demonstrations.
trend_en: Share halved (19 → 8); classic IRL and adversarial imitation were drawn off by VLAs and LLM preference learning, and remaining work turns to suboptimal demonstrations, language critiques and theoretical rates.

desc_en: Turning agent experience into reusable skills (text, code or parameters), studying skill evolution, composition, hierarchical organisation and continual internalisation.
trend_en: Exploded from zero in 2027 (2 → 56); once the Agent Skills paradigm spread, skills replaced raw trajectories as the basic unit of self-evolution, and work began on skill overfitting and access failures.

desc_en: Theory of disentangled and identifiable representation learning and representational similarity analysis; some papers are a grab-bag under a generic "representation learning" label.
trend_en: Stable (27 → 27); identifiability theory extends to relational data, task sparsity and multi-level hierarchies.

desc_en: Benchmarks of MLLM perception and reasoning: charts, maths, spatial, multi-image and domain knowledge.
trend_en: Plunged (71 → 20); general multimodal reasoning benchmarks saturated after the 2026 boom, and what remains in 2027 is mostly vertical-domain benchmarks (finance, species, floods) and failure diagnosis.

desc_en: Watermarking text and image generations, multi-bit watermarks, model fingerprints, and removal and forgery attacks on them.
trend_en: Down slightly (49 → 39); the focus moved from building new watermarks to forgery and removal attacks, public detectability and proofs of undetectability.

desc_en: Conformal prediction, risk control, selective prediction and anytime-valid inference, used to give finite-sample guarantees on model and agent outputs.
trend_en: Grew 4× (7 → 28); conformal risk control is being widely grafted onto auditing LLM reasoning, certifying agent trajectories and selectively delivering generated content.

desc_en: Benchmarks and evaluation frameworks for AI agents in terminal, web, office and professional workflows.
trend_en: Surged (22 → 51); after Terminal-Bench, benchmarks moved to professional workflows, company environments and end-to-end projects, with critiques arguing that "an agent is a system, not a model".

desc_en: Generative and sequential recommendation: semantic-ID item encoding, generative retrieval, cold start and LLM-based recommendation.
trend_en: Rising (43 → 50); generative recommendation replaced ID embeddings as the main line, with attention to SID learnability, parallel SID decoding and conflicting RL rewards.

desc_en: 3D human and hand pose, category-level and unseen-object 6D pose, and camera pose estimation.
trend_en: Stable (21 → 21); new work covers VLM-based 6DoF pose, single-reference unseen objects and event-camera pose.

desc_en: LLM weight quantization, vector and codebook quantization, and joint quantization-pruning-low-rank compression.
trend_en: Falling (21 → 12); gains from weight quantization alone are shrinking, and the focus moved to joint quantization, sparsity and low-rank methods and the details of rotation-based quantization.

desc_en: Indoor 3D scene generation and layout, scene-graph generation and manipulation, and building 3D scenes from a single image.
trend_en: Stable (32 → 31); moving from text-driven layout to compositional single-image construction, physical-feasibility correction and behavioural and functional grounding.

desc_en: Multi-agent RL, game theory, social dilemmas, opponent modelling and self-play.
trend_en: Share halved (27 → 14); classic MARL was drawn off by LLM multi-agent work, and remaining work covers social dilemmas, mean-field extensions and post-training effects on LLM cooperation.

desc_en: Prompt alignment, compositional generation, text rendering and aesthetic alignment in text-to-image generation, and evaluation benchmarks.
trend_en: Share nearly halved (59 → 34); T2I was drawn off by unified multimodal generation, and remaining work turns to fine-grained faithfulness such as counting, metaphors and implicit co-occurring objects.

desc_en: Indirect prompt injection against tool-using agents: attacks, defences, red-teaming and execution-boundary protection.
trend_en: Rising (25 → 39); moving from attacks and benchmarks to execution-boundary protection, memory-hijacking attacks and co-evolution of attack and defence.

desc_en: Pruning redundant visual tokens during VLM and MLLM inference, selected by attention, similarity or task relevance.
trend_en: Rising (16 → 28); methods moved from attention scoring to coverage, relational redundancy and sample-adaptive routing, and spilled over to VLAs.

desc_en: A miscellany grouped by the keyword "natural language processing"; the only coherent subtopics are text-to-SQL and formalising natural language.
trend_en: Plunged (40 → 11); generic papers self-labelled as "NLP" have nearly vanished, leaving interactive text-to-SQL reasoning and formal translation.

desc_en: Expressivity, memory and parallel training of sequence architectures such as Mamba/SSMs and linear RNNs.
trend_en: Falling (25 → 15); the "replace the Transformer" narrative has cooled, with work moving to state-tracking expressivity (non-abelian groups, quaternions) and parallelising nonlinear RNNs.

desc_en: Convergence and complexity lower bounds for stochastic, nonconvex and nonsmooth optimisation, and for bilevel and minimax optimisation.
trend_en: Stable (34 → 34); generalised smoothness, unbounded variance and bilevel optimisation with nonconvex lower levels remain the topics.

desc_en: A surface-level cluster grouped by the word "kernel": LLMs generating and optimising GPU kernels, mixed with NTK and kernel-method theory.
trend_en: Share recovered (25 → 28); almost all growth comes from agentic GPU-kernel optimisation and production-grade kernel benchmarks, while NTK and kernel methods themselves are shrinking.

desc_en: Stability, reward degradation, over-optimisation and heterogeneous-preference modelling for DPO and its variants, including preference alignment of diffusion models.
trend_en: Falling (54 → 33); offline DPO gave way to RLVR and online RL, and remaining work mostly patches DPO stability and over-optimisation theory.

desc_en: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN), embodied navigation benchmarks, and memory and reasoning supervision.
trend_en: Rising (35 → 56); VLN extends to air-ground collaboration, streaming constant-memory navigation and intent-driven long-horizon tasks, and adds reasoning supervision and self-improving harnesses.

desc_en: Authorisation, provenance, contracts, completion checks and state hand-off in the execution layer of tool-using agents; titles are highly uniform in wording, so part of this may be style clustering.
trend_en: From nothing to the largest cluster in this group (0.5 → 78); 2027 saw the rise of "agent runtime governance": authorisation and evidence checks for state-changing actions, monitoring that success ≠ completion, and patching harness flaws.

desc_en: MCMC, Langevin, importance and sequential Monte Carlo, and neural samplers driven by diffusion or transport.
trend_en: Recovering (20 → 28); Boltzmann sampling, replica exchange and amortised annealing driven by diffusion and transport maps are reviving.

desc_en: Building, retrieving and managing long-term memory for dialogue and LLM agents, with benchmarks such as LoCoMo.
trend_en: Grew 5× (10 → 48); memory became its own track, moving from memory construction to access policies, isolating interference across representations and evidence recall.

desc_en: Detecting AI-generated images and videos and deepfakes, with emphasis on generalisation across generators and interpretable forensics.
trend_en: Rising (32 → 44); focus on removing cross-generator shortcuts, with interpretable MLLM-based detection and AI-video detection on the rise.

desc_en: Knowledge graph completion, complex logical query answering, KG construction, and using KGs to constrain or augment LLM reasoning and factuality.
trend_en: Share nearly halved 42.4 → 23.7: growth in KG-RAG-style QA was drawn off by GraphRAG and agentic retrieval, and remaining work turns to KG foundation models (MERIT, ChainGram) and zero-shot queries of arbitrary structure.

desc_en: Constructing, detecting and purifying data-poisoning and trigger backdoors in image classification, federated learning, diffusion models and LLMs.
trend_en: Share down 47.4 → 33.9: backdoors in image classifiers are saturated, and new work centres on new attack surfaces such as LLM backdoor purification, quantization-conditioned backdoors and vertical federated learning.

desc_en: Association, identity memory and motion modelling in single- and multi-object tracking, tracking any point, and RGB-T and aerial tracking.
trend_en: Stable (14.1 → 15.1); novelty lies in memory-based resolution of identity conflicts, scaling open-vocabulary tracking with SSMs, and using tracking to probe object permanence in video world models.

desc_en: Designing VAEs and representation autoencoders for latent diffusion: diffusability, semantic alignment, and the link between reconstruction and generation quality; a few other "latent" papers are mixed in.
trend_en: Share down 43.9 → 32.3: the topic moved from "removing the VAE" and semantically disentangled VAEs to representation autoencoders (RAE), noise-aligned latent spaces and joint end-to-end training of the latent space.

desc_en: Removing the influence of specified data from trained models: approximate and certified unlearning, unlearning in federated and diffusion models, and evaluating unlearning.
trend_en: Share down 50.5 → 33.2: algorithmic innovation has slowed and the focus moved to rigorous evaluation: rethinking retraining as the gold standard, shadow-model-free evaluation, idempotent requests and uncertain forget sets.

desc_en: Predicting single-cell transcriptomic responses to genetic and drug perturbations to build "virtual cell" models, mostly with flow matching, Schrödinger bridges and graph models.
trend_en: Share grew about 4× (5.6 → 24.9): the Virtual Cell Challenge and large Perturb-seq datasets sparked a boom, alongside baseline critiques showing simple linear models can match and work on generalising to combinatorial perturbations.

desc_en: Open-vocabulary semantic, panoptic and 3D segmentation built on CLIP and VLMs, plus multimodal fusion and weakly supervised segmentation.
trend_en: Share up slightly 18.2 → 23.0: training-free OVSS (residuals, concept denoising) keeps being refined and extends to open-vocabulary segmentation of 3D point clouds and 3DGS scenes.

desc_en: Training and sampling of flow matching and rectified flow models: few-step and one-step generation, MeanFlow and flow maps, integrators and trajectory-drift correction.
trend_en: Share up 24.2 → 30.7: MeanFlow and flow maps became the main line for few-step generation, extending to pixel-space generation and continuous "flow language models" (self-conditioning).

desc_en: Membership inference attacks, dataset inference and training-data extraction, used to audit privacy leakage in LLMs, diffusion models and tabular generators.
trend_en: Share down 30.8 → 17.9: the community has started to question the reliability of MIA evaluation (confounding by distribution shift), and new targets are RL reasoning models and attention signals.

desc_en: Automatic prompt optimisation and prompt-sensitivity analysis for LLMs, mixed with older prompt-tuning work such as VLM prompt learning and visual reprogramming.
trend_en: Share halved 44.4 → 19.3: VLM soft-prompt learning is fading; remaining work diagnoses GEPA-style reflective prompt optimisation (what the reflector looks at, fixing saturation).

desc_en: Controllable diffusion-based image generation: style transfer, identity preservation, multi-subject reference generation, and layout and layer decomposition.
trend_en: Share halved 52.0 → 24.9: general MMDiT and unified editing models took over the space for task-specific adapters, leaving niches such as layer decomposition, panoramas and graphic design.

desc_en: MoE routing, load balancing, expert specialisation and sparsity control, and MoE in LoRA, diffusion and multimodal models.
trend_en: Share halved 45.9 → 20.2: small routing and load-balancing tweaks are saturated; new work moves to elastic compute, cross-layer expert sharing and bringing MoE to pixel diffusion and video editing.

desc_en: 3DGS/4DGS scene reconstruction, rendering, compression, relighting and editing, including feed-forward reconstruction and dynamic human avatars.
trend_en: Stable (64.6 → 60.4) and still one of the largest vision clusters; the focus moved from densification and speed to feed-forward relighting, cross-scale compression and structured latent spaces for 3D generation.

desc_en: Training LLM reasoning with verifiable rewards (RLVR/GRPO): reward design, advantage estimation, extension to non-verifiable domains and reward hacking.
trend_en: Share down 49.0 → 30.7: RLVR is now the default and has spread across subclusters; this cluster moved from "extending RLVR to open-ended tasks" to reward hacking, unreliable specifications and diagnosing gradient geometry.

desc_en: Post-hoc explanations such as SHAP and saliency maps, counterfactual and contrastive explanations, concept explanations, and evaluation of their faithfulness and robustness.
trend_en: Share fell to a third 40.9 → 13.5: classic XAI was replaced by mechanistic interpretability and SAEs, and the remainder leans toward formal explanation theory and benchmarks.

desc_en: Catastrophic forgetting in class-incremental and few-shot class-incremental learning: exemplar-free replay, prototypes, and incremental learning on CLIP-style pretrained models.
trend_en: Stable (18.7 → 17.9); nearly all methods build on frozen pretrained representations, with attention to exemplar-free drift compensation and neural-collapse geometry.

desc_en: Repository-level SWE agents and benchmarks: issue resolution, test generation, CI maintenance, whole-repository generation and harness design.
trend_en: Counts +50% but share 30.8 → 21.4: SWE-bench-style bug fixing is saturated, and benchmarks moved to continuous CI maintenance, generating whole repositories from scratch, tasks mined from vibe-coding sessions, and harness engineering.

desc_en: Confidence calibration of classifiers and LLMs/VLMs, verbalised confidence, selective prediction and uncertainty quantification over reasoning.
trend_en: Stable, slightly up (25.7 → 27.9); the focus moved to calibration loss caused by reasoning models and post-training (the "post-training tax") and calibrating verbalised confidence with rubrics and distillation.

desc_en: Visual reasoning in MLLMs and VLMs: R1-style RL, grounding in visual evidence, latent visual reasoning and "thinking with images".
trend_en: Share keeps growing 36.8 → 47.4: moving from copying GRPO to visual-evidence rewards, visual imagination and latent visual tokens, and native multimodal reasoning.

desc_en: Structural causal models, identifiability of causal representations, counterfactual inference, causal abstraction and root-cause analysis.
trend_en: Share down slightly 29.8 → 24.4; new trends are causal foundation models (amortised structure and effect prediction) and learning identifiable world models from pretrained diffusion representations.

desc_en: A mixed cluster grouped by generic "deep neural networks" wording: network theory, activation functions, hypergraph networks, CNN feature learning and more.
trend_en: Share collapsed 74.7 → 19.1: likely a wording artefact, since 2027 papers use LLM and Transformer vocabulary rather than "DNN"; what remains is mostly classic theory such as width/depth separation.

desc_en: Context compression, folding, memory and state management for long-horizon LLM agents, so that evidence is not lost over long trajectories.
trend_en: Share up 5× (7.1 → 37.0): after ACON and Context Folding, context compression became its own subfield, now studying verification of compression, semantic hand-off and task-progress mismatch.

desc_en: Autoregressive mesh generation, text- and sketch-to-CAD, part-aware and simulation-ready articulated asset generation, with a few avatar and geometric-graph generation papers.
trend_en: Share up 22.2 → 33.2: moving from artist-mesh generation to executable CAD (LLM code plus RL from execution feedback) and part-based, articulated assets for simulation.
